version.changelog: v2.0.1: Fixed SKILL.md name field, minor doc updates

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: vikunja-task-api
Version: 2.0.1

The skill is a legitimate integration for the Vikunja task management system, providing a bash CLI helper (vikunja.sh) and agent instructions (SKILL.md) to manage projects and tasks. It uses standard environment variables (VIKUNJA_URL, VIKUNJA_TOKEN) for configuration and authentication, and its operations are strictly limited to the Vikunja API. While the bash script lacks robust JSON escaping for task titles, this is a minor functional bug rather than a security vulnerability or malicious behavior. No evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized execution, or malicious prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill is internally coherent: it only requires curl/jq, a Vikunja base URL and a Vikunja token (or username/password fallback) and its instructions and script only call the Vikunja API endpoints described.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (Vikunja task management) aligns with the declared requirements (curl, jq, VIKUNJA_URL, VIKUNJA_TOKEN) and the included script implements only Vikunja API calls (projects, tasks, login). Minor metadata inconsistencies exist (SKILL.md metadata and registry file show slightly different versions/owner IDs and SKILL.md treats token as optional while registry lists it as primary), but these do not change the functional alignment.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and vikunja.sh instruct only to call Vikunja endpoints and to use VIKUNJA_TOKEN or perform a login to $VIKUNJA_URL/login. There are no commands to read unrelated system files or to post data to third-party endpoints. Examples include an internal example IP but that is only illustrative.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or remote downloads are present; this is an instruction-only skill with a bundled shell script. Nothing is being fetched or written to disk by an installer step outside the user's control.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Requested environment access is proportionate: VIKUNJA_URL and a Vikunja credential (VIKUNJA_TOKEN preferred; VIKUNJA_USERNAME/PASSWORD supported as fallback). The token is sensitive; SKILL.md recommends storing env vars in a secure file. No unrelated credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and does not request system-wide persistent configuration or modify other skills. It can be invoked autonomously (platform default), which is expected for a callable integration; this combined with possession of a token means the agent can make API calls to the configured Vikunja instance when the skill runs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do only what it says, but review these practical points before installing: 1) Confirm VIKUNJA_URL points to the intended Vikunja instance (the examples include an internal IP—ensure you don't accidentally point the skill at an internal service you didn't intend to share). 2) Provide a least-privilege API token (VIKUNJA_TOKEN) rather than your full admin credentials where possible; if you use username/password the script will POST them to $VIKUNJA_URL/login to obtain a token. 3) Store the token in a secure environment (do not paste into public logs). 4) Review the included vikunja.sh locally (it is short and readable) before enabling the skill. 5) Because the agent can invoke skills autonomously by default, be aware the agent will be able to use the token to call your Vikunja instance when this skill runs; revoke the token if you suspect misuse. 6) Note minor metadata/version mismatches in the package (owner/version fields differ), which is not functionally concerning but worth checking if provenance matters to you.
